solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fall of rascal in lawsuit

indicators.note: the rascal sits within the lawsuit, so one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: a lawsuit is a legal case
a cad is a dishonourable rascal

explanation.surface: Someone reports the downfall of a scoundrel caught up in litigation.
explanation.definitionFit: A cascade is a waterfall, a fall of water down rocks.

clue.text: Church holding a service in which wine may be served

definitions.text: in which wine may be served

indicators.note: the church abbreviation wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
the RAF, Royal Air Force, is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: A church service where communion wine is offered.
explanation.definitionFit: A carafe is a glass jug for serving wine or water at table.

clue.text: Initially going after single run, ultimately getting a bye

indicators.note: after places the first letter of going behind the other pieces

parts.note: solo means single or alone

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of run
initially points to the first letter of going

explanation.surface: Cricket talk: a batsman gets going with a single, finally scoring a bye.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bye is a run scored without the batsman hitting the ball; here it means goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: So long is an informal farewell, the same as saying bye.

clue.text: Article rebel was wrong to blame

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: wrong means the letters are put out of their proper order

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece says the rebel was mistaken and at fault.
explanation.definitionFit: Being answerable means being responsible, so the one to blame for something.

clue.text: Kennedy regularly against being aligned with the Observer?

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of Kennedy

parts.note: on can mean against or touching, as in leaning on a wall

explanation.surface: Kennedy repeatedly opposing a partnership with the Observer newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Observer' looks like the British Sunday newspaper, but it means anyone watching.
explanation.definitionFit: End-on describes something with its end facing the viewer, so lined up with an observer's sightline.

clue.text: Little male that's cold, consumed by hatred

indicators.note: the cold letter is swallowed up inside the word for hatred

parts.note: odium is widespread hatred or disgust
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A small man whose coldness is eaten away by loathing.
explanation.definitionFit: A modicum is a small amount, so 'little' works as a noun: a little of something.

clue.text: Note emblem held by North African dignitary

indicators.note: the North African grips the other pieces inside

parts.note: a Moor is a person from north-west Africa
a sign is a symbol or emblem

explanation.surface: A North African grandee holding a badge and a written note.
explanation.definitionFit: A monsignor is a senior Roman Catholic cleric, an ecclesiastical dignitary.

clue.text: Act up just the same?

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from the bottom, and the word is unchanged that way

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A request to misbehave in the same way again.
explanation.definitionFit: A deed is an act or action someone performs.

clue.text: Discovered infant in hold — utterly horrifying

indicators.note: the uncovered infant is placed within the word for hold

parts.note: to cling is to grip tightly

indicators.note: discovered means uncovered, so the infant word loses its outer letters

parts.note: a child is an infant

explanation.surface: A baby found in a ship's hold, a dreadful discovery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discovered' reads as found, but it means stripped of its covering: CHILD loses C and D to leave HIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Chilling means frightening enough to make the blood run cold.

clue.text: City brass without end, almost

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so money surrounds the other piece

parts.note: brass is British slang for money

indicators.note: almost drops the final letter of the end word

parts.note: a term is an end or limit, as of a period

explanation.surface: A town's brass band playing on almost without stopping.
explanation.definitionFit: Monterey is a coastal city in California.

clue.text: Classy car drives forward

definitions.meaning: the ...-Royce, a luxury British car, is colloquially called a ...
to roll is to move forward on wheels, so this is the verb form

explanation.surface: A posh motor surges ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Rolls is short for Rolls-Royce, the luxury car maker, and also the verb for moving on wheels.

clue.text: Working lad, done in, is a weed

indicators.note: working here means worked over or reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boy toiling until exhausted, apparently a useless person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weed' looks like an insult for the feeble lad, but it names a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The dandelion is a common yellow-flowered lawn weed.

clue.text: Identify secure digital connection

parts.note: to finger someone is to identify them to the police
to nail something is to fasten it securely

explanation.surface: It reads like a request to pin down a secure link in computing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digital' suggests computers, but it means attached to a digit.
explanation.definitionFit: The nail grows from and is joined to a finger, a digit of the hand.

clue.text: Feel good harbouring this emotion?

indicators.note: the question mark is the only signal that the concealed letters must be read right to left; no word in the clue says so
the words feel good hold the answer within their letters, as a harbour holds a ship

explanation.surface: Feeling good while sheltering a certain mood.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit in 'Feel good' read right to left, but the clue as printed has no reversal word; only the question mark hints at it, a lapse by the setter.
explanation.definitionFit: Glee is delight or joy, the emotion that comes with feeling good.

clue.text: His output may well have been flagging

definitions.text: His output may well have been flagging

parts.words: His output may well have been flagging
parts.note: flagging is paving with flagstones, and a stone well is another product of this craftsman

explanation.surface: A worker whose production may have been tailing off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flagging' looks like tiring, but it means paving with flagstones; 'may well' hides a stone well too.
explanation.definitionFit: A mason who works in stone cuts flagstones for paving and could build a well.

clue.text: Fellow writer getting caught out by attitude that wasn't planned

indicators.note: out tells us the caught letter is removed from the fellow

parts.note: a chap is a fellow
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a pen is a writing implement
a stance is a position or attitude

explanation.surface: An author's fellow is caught out by a stance that arose by accident.
explanation.definitionFit: Happenstance is coincidence, something that occurs by chance rather than design.

clue.text: Work rejected, I see, in terribly noisy, hazardous plant

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the work abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work

indicators.note: the I and see pieces go into the jumbled noisy
terribly signals the letters of noisy are thrown into disorder

parts.note: V is short for vide, Latin for see

explanation.surface: A rejected work, terribly noisy, and a dangerous factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terribly' jumbles NOISY into ISONY, and 'in' puts I and V inside it before the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Poison ivy is a North American plant whose leaves cause a painful rash.

clue.text: Moved punctually given support of journalist

indicators.note: in a down clue the journalist sits beneath and supports the first piece

parts.note: prompt can mean exactly on time, as in at six prompt
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter shifted on time with an editor's backing.
explanation.definitionFit: Prompted means moved or spurred to action.

clue.text: Old maid, the first to be withdrawn following row

indicators.note: following puts the reversed piece after the row word

parts.note: to scull is to row with oars

indicators.note: withdrawn means drawn back, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: the first is No. 1, written as NO plus I

explanation.surface: An elderly spinster, the first to leave after an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel, but it is rowing a boat; 'the first' is No. 1, NOI.
explanation.definitionFit: A scullion was a kitchen servant doing menial work, an old word for a maid.

clue.text: Being obstinate, managed to stop extremely curt article being rewritten

indicators.note: the managed word plugs the middle of the jumble, like a stopper in a bottle
rewriting the letters puts them in a new order
extremely points to the outer letters of curt

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business

explanation.surface: Someone stubbornly gets a terse piece of writing redrafted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop' suggests halting, but here it means plugging a gap, as a stopper fills a bottle neck.
explanation.definitionFit: Recalcitrant means stubbornly uncooperative, an adjective for someone being obstinate.

clue.text: Place for housing estate?

parts.note: estate means an estate car here, and housing means storing rather than a residential development

explanation.surface: A site for a residential development.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain an estate is a station wagon, a car with a large rear load space.
explanation.definitionFit: A garage is the building where a car such as an estate is kept.

clue.text: Break depression

definitions.meaning: a break or pause, as in a school or parliamentary interval
a hollow or alcove set back into a wall

explanation.definitionFit: A recess is both an interval in work and an indentation set back into a surface.

clue.text: An island to ponder

definitions.meaning: an island in the Scottish Inner Hebrides
to ... something over is to consider it

explanation.surface: An island to sit and think about.
explanation.definitionFit: Mull is a large island off western Scotland, and to mull is to think something over.

clue.text: Perfect 3-D object filled by something local?

indicators.note: the solid shape is packed with the dialect word placed inside it

parts.note: a cone is a three-dimensional solid
summat is northern English dialect for something

explanation.surface: An ideal solid packed with some regional product.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' signals a regional dialect word: SUMMAT is how 'something' is said in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Consummate as an adjective means complete or supremely skilled, so perfect in quality.

clue.text: Runs away from scraps — takes off

indicators.note: the runs letter goes away from the scraps word

parts.note: shreds are scraps or tatters
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone flees from scrap pieces and departs.
explanation.definitionFit: To shed is to take off or cast off, as clothes or skin.

clue.text: Polish finally warding off defeat

indicators.note: off means removed, so the letter is taken from the polish word

parts.note: gloss is a shine or polish

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of warding

explanation.surface: A Polish side finally holding off a defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality but means shine.
explanation.definitionFit: A loss is a defeat in a game or contest.

clue.text: Fossil I behold with black, dull exterior

indicators.note: the dull word forms an outside layer around the other pieces

parts.note: trite means dull and overused
lo is an old word meaning look or behold
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone gazes at a dark, dreary-looking relic from the rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Trilobites are extinct marine arthropods whose fossils are common in ancient rocks.

clue.text: Time to stop glut, say

indicators.note: the time letter plugs the gap in the word for glut

parts.note: to glut and to sate both mean to fill to excess

explanation.surface: A call for time to end overindulgence.
explanation.definitionFit: To state is to say or declare, so the verb fits as a synonym.

clue.text: Vacated dirty and filthy house?

indicators.note: emptying the word dirty leaves only its first and last letters

parts.note: nasty means filthy or foul

explanation.surface: An empty, grimy, squalid home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' reads as a building, but it means a ruling family, as in the House of Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynasty is a line of rulers from one family, also called a royal house.

clue.text: Children will absorb clear forms of poetry

indicators.note: the children take the clear word into their middle

parts.note: sons are male children
net means clear, as in net profit after deductions

explanation.surface: Kids will soak up a plain understanding of verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonnets are fourteen-line poems, a classic verse form.
